articles.description:
Decide What a Model May Draft Before It Writes: A Section Ownership Gate for Docs


A model-drafted page fails in one of two ways: it invents a fact, or it quietly overstates a promise your team cannot keep. The first failure is cheap to catch, because somebody can check a fact against a source file. The second one survives review for months, because the sentence sounds exactly like the ones your best technical writer produces.
So the useful question before drafting is not "is this paragraph good?" but "was a model allowed to write this paragraph at all?". That answer depends on consequences rather than on style: a changelog entry can be wrong and fixed on Monday, while a compatibility guarantee is a promise other people plan their quarter around.
The gate below encodes that decision in th…
articles.title: Decide What a Model May Draft Before It Writes: A Section Ownership Gate for Docs

My Fast Movers has 27,854 route pages (every state-to-state moving corridor, e.g. Texas to California). Programmatic SEO at that scale has one mortal enemy: duplicate content. Here's how we keep every page genuinely unique.

articles.author: StarkMan
articles.description:
DPoP makes a token sender-constrained, which changes what a stolen token is worth


Every bearer token in an OAuth deployment carries the same implicit promise: whoever holds the string can use it. That promise is what makes a leaked access token useful to an attacker and awkward for a defender. Revoking a token works, but revocation is a reaction. The better question is whether a token can be made useless to anyone who merely copies it. Demonstrating Proof of Possession, standardised as RFC 9449, is the practical answer that has reached general adoption.
A bearer token is a credential in the same sense a session cookie is. If it appears in a log, a browser extension, a misconfigured proxy cache, a crash dump, or a support ticket, it is usable until it expires or is revoked. The OAuth 2.0 …
articles.title: DPoP makes a token sender-constrained, which changes what a stolen token is worth

I Built My Own Sync Gateway Instead of Using Couchbase. Here's How.


Push queues, pull checkpoints, safe conflict merges, and keeping secrets off the wire. All from a real offline-first healthcare app.
When we started on the offline sync for our healthcare app, I seriously considered Couchbase Sync Gateway and Firestore. Both are good. Both handle offline sync well for most apps.
Then we wrote down our constraints:
Doctors in remote clinics with no signal for hours
Patient records where an allergy can never be silently overwritten
PIN hashes and recovery secrets that must never leave the device they were created on
The whole backend has to run on a laptop in a clinic, with no cloud
That last one settled it. We built our own.
Two stores, one protocol. The phone has SQLite with a full local…

articles.author: Dakota Huang
articles.description:
Most refactors fail in review, not in the compiler. The diff is too wide for anyone to read carefully. AI assistants make that worse: one prompt can return 900 changed lines. So put a budget on the diff before you argue about tests.
This post is one script and one table. The script measures what a branch actually touches. The table declares how much surface each refactor type may touch. You run the script on every commit. If the branch exceeds the budget, you split the branch.
A passing suite tells you behavior survived. It says nothing about review load. A 40-file diff with green tests still gets rubber-stamped at 5pm.
Three numbers predict review failure better than test count:
files touched
added plus deleted lines
public symbol churn (renames, moved exports, signature changes)
Track th…
articles.title: Set a Change Budget Before You Refactor: A Git-Diff Gate for Messy Repos

With 56,000 games on Gameziko, search is easy. Discovery is the hard part. Nobody types what they want when they don't know it exists. Here's what we learned building categories people actually browse.
Our first category page was an alphabetical list. It tested terribly. Users scrolled, got overwhelmed, and left. The fix wasn't fewer games, it was better doors into the catalog.
We now treat categories as answers to moods, not genres. "Puzzle" is a genre. "Games you can finish on a coffee break" is a mood. Mood-based groupings consistently outperform genre lists in click-through, sometimes 3 to 1.
A few patterns from our analytics:
Session length beats game count. Categories with 50 well-chosen games outperform categories with 500 unsorted ones. Curation is a feature.

articles.author: Finley Zhou
articles.description:
A test result is a claim about a machine, not a claim about a patch.
When an agent hands you a diff plus a green suite, the suite ran somewhere. That somewhere had a Python version, a locale, a timezone, a case-sensitive filesystem, and a set of installed package versions. Change any of those and a subset of your assertions changes meaning. The patch didn't get better or worse — the evidence moved.
This article is about fixing that with a small, reproducible artifact: a portability ledger. It answers one question per test — does this green survive a second machine? — and refuses to let environment drift hide behind a passing CI badge.
It is deliberately not about flaky-test freezing policy, diff coverage, or mutation strength. Those are separate ledgers. This one only measures whether your…
articles.title: Your Agent Patch's Green Didn't Travel: A Portability Ledger for Two-Machine Test Evidence

articles.description:
Three cybersecurity lessons from Middle-earth: trust, concentrated power and resilience.
A tower. A silent chamber. A dark stone lights up with armies, cities and distant fires. Whoever watches it has something irresistible: the feeling of seeing what others cannot see.
It looks like an absolute advantage. Then comes the uncomfortable question: are you understanding the world, or is someone deciding which part of it you get to see?
The Palantír is a surprisingly modern temptation. It promises visibility and puts information in front of decision-makers. A security dashboard does something similar, although it usually does not contain the Eye of Sauron. Usually.
The Lord of the Rings is not a cybersecurity manual. But three of its images help us ask better questions: a stone that shows, a ri…
articles.title: The Palantír Does Not Lie. But Who Controls What You See?

Yooooooo... wassup developers!! How are you all?? 😭
So, still no new users... which means old stats = new stats 😂
Today is Day 16 of building my project, a social media platform named Crowdwide, standing at 11 users and 40+ posts.
So, I feel like there is no need to add new features just to maintain the flow. Now, I need to focus on getting users onto the platform!
To make login and signup easier for users, I added the GitHub login/create account option to Crowdwide.
And nothing much new is there...
Also, I got 12+ emails from other companies and 4+ from YouTubers for promoting Crowdwide. I accepted only 2 out of all of them.
I mean, I'm building everything with a 0 budget. That's why 😭 I'm 15, and I can't make payments.
And out of those two, one is building a startup/website platform, and he agreed to a partnership with Crowdwide!
That's the first time I've ever gotten a partnership with any platform or website owner. 🥹
I also applied to some platforms to get a parent-child monetization system for Crowdwide.
Like:
Crowdwide platform → Communities under Crowdwide get monetized → Community owners earn money.
But the platforms providing this require a large amount of traffic and so many other things...
The thing I need most at this moment is USERS! 😭
Also, from the stats, I got to know that Sunday is when most Crowdwide users revisit the platform!!
YEAAAAAAAA!! 🔥
According to the stats, I think most of them are coming from the newsletter, but they still come back, like a few posts, make some comments, and engage!
I've noticed that Saturday and Sunday are the best days for promoting posts, articles, polls, and communities.
It works well!
BTW, if you have any ideas or thoughts, you can share them! I'll definitely discuss them.
Links:
Crowdwide: https://www.crowdwide.run.place/
Open source: https://github.com/DeveloperPuneet/Crowdwide
